verdict.rationale: The evidence pack describes Skills as capability-packaging (SKILL.md files, plugins, marketplaces) that Claude loads into context during an active session, not as a mechanism for scheduling or triggering autonomous background automations. While adjacent Claude Code features like 'Agent view' (background sessions) and 'Agent teams' are mentioned, none of this is tied to Skills setting up autonomous background runs — Skills require Claude to be actively working and decide (often unreliably per community reports) whether to invoke them. Missing for 10: any documentation of Skills triggering scheduled/unattended background automations, or evidence linking Skills specifically to the background/agent-view features. [2026-09-30 judge-migration owner-product bias audit: reverted opus-5-5 partial q3 -> the committed sonnet-5 baseline none q0. The rationale concedes skills are not a scheduling or background runtime; the credit rests on a marketing phrase, relevance-based auto-loading (which cited community reports call hit-or-miss), and the host product's agent view — none of which is a background automation the user sets up. Anthropic-affiliation governance, README §9.]
